claim.quote: The effectiveness of the WIMP model independent annual modulation signature is pointed out by discussing the results obtained over 7 annual cycles (107731 kg day total exposure); the WIMP presence in the galactic halo is strongly supported at 6.3 standard deviation C.L.

key_value.note: Total exposure of the seven annual cycles.

name: Dark Matter search
notes: Result type 'measurement': the abstract says the WIMP presence is 'strongly supported'; it does not use the word 'evidence' (the 2003 conference summary of the same data does, see the next record).

significance.quote: strongly supported at 6.3 standard deviation C.L.

summary.plain: DAMA's final report on its 100 kg sodium iodide detector: seven years of data in which the counting rate rises and falls with the seasons. The team says this strongly supports a dark matter halo around our galaxy, at 6.3 standard deviations. Other experiments have not reproduced it.
summary.technical: Review of the DAMA/NaI results: seven annual cycles, 107731 kg day; the data favour a cosine-like modulation (period one year, phase near 2 June) of the single-hit residual rate in the 2-6 keV region; the abstract's wording is 'strongly supported at 6.3 standard deviation C.L.'; the paper also examines model-dependent WIMP scenarios.

title: Dark Matter search
why_it_matters: The headline DAMA/NaI claim, which DAMA/LIBRA continued and which ANAIS, COSINE, SABRE, DM-Ice and PICOLON were built to test with the same target.
